newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Volatility trades struck in FTSE index.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Volatility trades struck in FTSE index.

text.p: A flurry of volatility trades dominated dealings in FTSE 100 index options as the London stock market slid down on Thursday, dealers said.

The idea behind the deals is to buy/sell options in the index and to hedge them by an appropriate position in FTSE futures. Over a given time period, market direction will not matter so much as a change in volatility to produce a profit.

One such deal was from a buyer of 500 December 3725 puts at 59p, who also bought December futures at 3959. Another trader, also expecting implied volatility to increase, bought 500 October 3850 puts at 33p against September futures at 3929.

More sophisticated were deals involving long strangles against short futures. One such deal was to buy 500 December 3500 puts as well as 500 December 4125 calls for a net debit of 43p against selling December futures at 3943.
By 1505 GMT, the cash index was down 34.1 at 3884.6, while September futures had lost 45 point to 3896 and December futures were 43.5 points worse off at 3919.
In stock options one broker bought 1,250 February 200 calls in oil and gas explorer Lasmo and managed to cross 1,000 lots.

In the food retailing sector, the main trade in Tesco was from a buyer of 675 November puts at 8-1/2p and 9p. And in Asda Group the January 110 calls were busy with one trader selling a total of 1,000 lots at 8p and 8-1/2p.
Tesco shares tumbled 10p to 301p and Asda was 4-1/4p down at 110-1/4p.
In conglomerate Hanson, there was a buyer of 3,500 November 180 calls at 1-1/2p. The shares fell 5p to 156p.
